sources.entry: Apple On-Device OpenAI - Runs Apple on-device models behind an OpenAI-compatible API. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/gety-ai/apple-on-device-openai) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: A SwiftUI macOS app that runs Apple's on-device Foundation Models behind an OpenAI-compatible local API server.
summary.what_it_does: The app starts a local HTTP server (default 127.0.0.1:11535) that exposes OpenAI-style endpoints: GET /health, GET /status, GET /v1/models, and POST /v1/chat/completions. The chat completions endpoint supports both streaming and non-streaming responses. It checks Apple Intelligence availability on startup and reports model status through /status. Requests are served by Apple's on-device Foundation Models, so processing stays local. The README lists temperature, max_tokens, stream, model, and messages as the supported parameters. A Python test script (test_server.py) covers health checks, multi-turn chat, Chinese-language input, and streaming. Tool/function calling is listed as work in progress.
use_cases: Use Apple on-device AI with OpenAI-compatible apps
Run local chat completions without a cloud API key
Test OpenAI SDK code against a local model
Stream local LLM responses to a client app
Check Apple Intelligence availability from a script
how_to_run: Download the latest .zip from the Releases page, extract it, and launch the app
Or clone the repository and run: open AppleOnDeviceOpenAI.xcodeproj
Build and run the project in Xcode
In the app, set the server address (default 127.0.0.1:11535) and click Start Server
Point an OpenAI client at the server with base_url set to the local address and model set to apple-on-device
Run python3 test_server.py while the server is running to verify it
notable: Wraps Apple's on-device Foundation Models in an OpenAI Chat Completions-compatible API
Built as a GUI app, not a CLI, to avoid the rate limit Apple applies to command-line tools (per the README's cited Apple DTS quote)
Supports streaming responses in OpenAI's streaming format
Ships a test script that exercises health, status, SDK compatibility, multi-turn, Chinese, and streaming
caveats: Requires macOS 26 beta 2 and Xcode 26 beta 2 for building, per the README
Requires Apple Intelligence to be enabled in system settings
Rate limits may still occur; the README says to restart the server if they do
Tool using/function calling is marked work in progress
